newsitem.title: TURKEY: Members of Turk Moslem sect mark riot anniversary.
newsitem.headline: Members of Turk Moslem sect mark riot anniversary.

text.p: Thousands of people marched through a run-down Istanbul district on Wednesday to mark the second anniversary of riots by Turkey's Alevi Moslem community during which 17 people were killed in clashes with police.

"The Gazi people are here, where are the murderers?" the residents of the mainly Alevi Gazi district chanted as they marched through its narrow main street to the cemetery where the victims of the riots were buried.
Many of the demonstrators wore red headbands or sported red ribbons usually associated with the liberal Alevi sect.
A police helicopter hovered overhead and hundreds of riot police stood by as the protesters filed past.

Angry demonstrators, most from the Alevi community, clashed with police on March 12, 1995 after unknown gunmen shot dead two people in attacks on four coffee houses and a pastry shop in Gazi -- all establishments known for their Alevi patrons.
Some 20 policemen were arrested for their alleged rough handling of the riots but their trial has been moved out of Istanbul and there have been no convictions yet.
Victims' families blame the police for the killings. Television pictures showed police firing into the crowds.
"We are crying out to the world -- the murderers must be tried. The murderers are within the state," Cemal Poyraz, the father of victim Zeynep, told Reuters.
"Two years have gone by but nothing has been done to the murderers."
The organisers of Wednesday's event said more than 20,000 protesters had turned up to the march. Police would not comment on the numbers.
Turkey's Alevis practise a relaxed form of Islam which has often made them the target of hardline Islamists among the country's majority Sunni Moslems.
